extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of Stoicism; readers who want to write or follow a personal Stoic handbook
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, actionable guidance for composing and living by a personal handbook of Stoic practices: daily exercises, time management, meditations on impermanence, and ethical rules for friendship and virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily exercise: state the nature of seductive/things
rubrics_metrics.description: On each of the seductive things, which are suitable for use or which are loved, remember to say what is their nature, starting with the smallest things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if you like a clay pot, say 'I like a clay pot' so you will not be troubled if it breaks; when kissing your child or spouse, remind yourself they are a human being so you can bear the fact of their mortality. This mental labelling trains detachment and reduces disturbance when externals change or are lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage time: recognize that life seems brief only when wasted
rubrics_metrics.description: Seneca’s four premises: (1) life is only brief if time is not well employed; (2) many claim to want leisure but are overwhelmed by occupations; (3) some who seem idle shorten their lives by excessive pleasures or sterile pursuits; (4) true leisure devoted to philosophical study elevates the person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: regard time as a scarce resource to be guarded and invested in philosophic study and true leisure rather than dissipated on trivial pleasures, pedantry, or endless busyness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical time-management steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete advice to take control of your time by auditing and reorganizing how you spend it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) Make a list of places/contexts where you spend time weekly; (2) Reflect which places/activities waste time or offer no benefit to spiritual development or mental health; (3) Reorganize your time: reserve portions for reading philosophy and self-reflection, set weekly hours for physical exercise (long walks, bike rides), eliminate or minimize conversations that bring nothing positive, and avoid places where time is wasted. Anti-pattern: allowing others to take significant portions of your life without scruple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meditate daily on impermanence and the brevity of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Constant meditation on the impermanence and brevity of all things and on the limited time allotted to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: creates an inner discourse that leads to living more intensely, valuing loved ones, and acting with urgency. Do this not morbidly but as a reminder to live fully. Use memorized quotes and short maxims to reinforce this habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept externals as not under our control (Epictetus’ Ontological Theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish what depends on us (our opinions, impulses, assent, choice) from what does not (possessions, reputation, positions, even our bodies and loved ones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice: treat possessions and roles as loaned (the inn metaphor)—when lost, say they have been returned. This reduces attachment, prepares for losses (fires, thefts, job loss), and fosters equanimity. Anti-pattern: treating externals as permanent or fully owned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemplate death as natural and use it to foster gratitude and full living
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize death as a natural part of life; the body and even our memory are temporary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome: contemplations of mortality should make life feel precious and spur gratitude and fuller living rather than melancholia. Practice daily meditation on mortality to remove fear and encourage immediate, meaningful action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate true friendship (non-utilitarian, virtuous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship is a mutual impulse of attraction and duty; true friends are those who contribute objectively to making your life better and whom you could, metaphorically, follow into exile or die for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with temporary/useful friendships that vanish when benefits cease. True friendship is not commerce; it involves mutual affection, moral support, and shared pursuit of the good. Anti-pattern: mistaking flattering or self-interested acquaintances for friends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate friends by actions and objective contribution, not declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate sincere friends from flatterers and manipulators by observing whether they materially improve and contribute to your life rather than merely saying 'I love you'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques: sharpen observation, check whether friends attend to your needs or only to what you offer, see if they offer honest criticism that helps your moral progress, and do not remain in relationships out of fear of loneliness. Use adversaries’ criticism as a tool for self-awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use criticism (even from enemies) for self-awareness and moral progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn from criticisms and opposition as they may reveal truths you have not yet accepted and can be instrumental for self-improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss adversarial observations automatically; test their truth, extract useful truths, and use them to correct false opinions or bad habits. Anti-pattern: reflexively rejecting any critique because it is unpleasant or comes from an opponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against being 'busy'—reserve time for yourself and wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the condition of being constantly occupied by others’ demands, which steals your life; plan each day as if it were your last and reserve time for yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who plan and reserve their time make their lives long in value. Anti-patterns include living to others' rhythms ('sleep someone else's sleep') or postponing living until some future age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice philosophical teachings daily in speech and action
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely holding opinions is insufficient; one must speak them and practice them daily for them to have effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular repetition and practice of Stoic precepts—saying, hearing, and living them—deepens their impact. Example: Epictetus’ fragments emphasizing constant practice. Anti-pattern: intellectualizing Stoicism without exercising it in life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue self-mastery through mental and physical exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop enkrateia (self-mastery or self-government) via exercises of mental and physical strengthening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-mastery is cultivated by deliberate practices—habitual reflection, restraining impulses, physical discipline—that increase resistance to passions. Teachers and students are 'progressers' working toward the ideal sage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate the cardinal virtues as the sole proper human good
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to develop prudence (phronesis), courage (andreia), temperance (sophrosyne), and justice (dikaiosyne); virtue is knowledge of good and bad and the human good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and roles: prudence = knowledge of good and bad; courage = correct knowledge of fear; temperance = knowing what to endure; justice = knowledge of what is due. The Stoic ethical program centers on these as the standard for actions and evaluations. Use them as benchmarks when reorganizing time, choosing friends, and responding to externals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test opinions and withdraw assent from false representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion (dogma/hypolepsis) must be tested; assent is the act by which truth is attributed to a representation and should be withheld or withdrawn if found false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice critical examination of impressions (phantasiai) before assenting; cultivate the capacity of choice (prohairesis) to control impulses and judgments. Anti-pattern: granting immediate assent to every impression, leading to passion and error.
